threads.thread_goal: Align on target account list and pilot scope for the new device program.

messages.text: Team, we're kicking off the new medical device education and sales program. We have 21 days to get the pilot ready. First priority: let's lock down which accounts we're targeting and what priority tiers make sense. I've started a rough list but want input from everyone on geography, specialty mix, and which accounts are most receptive. Can we use A1 (Target Account Segmentation Sheet) to collaborate? Let me know your top 5 accounts by EOD tomorrow.

Good kickoff. I've reviewed the initial list and it looks solid geographically. One thing to flag: we should segment by specialty because the messaging will differ between orthopedic and general surgery accounts. Also, I'd suggest we cap the pilot at 8-10 accounts max so we can gather quality feedback before scaling. That gives us enough volume without spreading too thin.

Agree on the specialty split. I'd add that we should prioritize accounts where we already have a relationship or a champion. That'll help with adoption. I can pull together a list of our strongest contacts by region if that helps.
I'll add my accounts to the sheet. Not sure which ones are the best fit though. Should I just list everyone I know or do you want me to focus on specific regions?

Let's focus on the top 3 regions first—Northeast, Midwest, and Southeast. For each account, note the specialty, your relationship strength (strong/medium/new), and whether they've shown interest in new device categories. That'll help us prioritize. 70832, can you help 63661 with the criteria?

Absolutely. 63661, I'll send you a quick template with the scoring logic. Basically: strong relationships get priority, then we look at specialty alignment and past adoption patterns. Once we have all the data in A1, we can rank them and propose the final pilot list.

I've added my accounts to the sheet. Most of mine are in the Southeast and Midwest. I think we should also consider accounts that have been slow to adopt in the past—they might benefit most from the education angle. Just a thought.

Good point. Let's include a mix—some early adopters for quick wins and some that need more education. That'll give us a balanced pilot. Can everyone confirm their entries in A1 are complete by tomorrow EOD? Then I'll consolidate and we'll make the final call on which 8-10 we're targeting.
I'll have mine finalized by EOD. One more thing—should we assign account owners now or wait until we finalize the list?
Let's wait until we lock the list. That way we can assign based on geography and existing relationships. Once we approve D1 and D2, we'll do the owner assignments in the same meeting.
Sounds good. I'll also start drafting the webinar topics based on the account specialties we're seeing. That way we can tailor the education content to what each group needs most.
OK, I'll get my data in the sheet tomorrow. Thanks for the template.

Perfect. Let's reconvene tomorrow afternoon once all entries are in. I'll send a summary of the consolidated list and we'll vote on the final 8-10 accounts and confirm D1 and D2. This will lock our scope and let the rest of the team move forward on content and training.

threads.thread_goal: Review and finalise educational slide deck and sales script.

messages.text: I've drafted the clinician-focused educational slide deck (A2) covering indications, mechanism, benefits and safety. The deck is structured for both webinars and in-person visits. All claims are sourced from the approved clinical data. Before we send this to regulatory for review, I'd like feedback from the sales team on messaging clarity and whether the objection-handling angles make sense. 36427, 438092—can you review and flag anything that feels off or missing?

I've reviewed A2. The structure is solid and the clinical narrative flows well. One thing: the safety section is thorough but might be dense for a live presentation. Could we add a quick summary slide at the end that clinicians can take away? Also, I'd suggest we add a slide on cost-effectiveness early—that's always the first question we get.

Good catches. I'll add a summary slide and move the health economics content earlier. On cost-effectiveness, I want to make sure we're only citing approved data—let me check with medical affairs on what claims we can make there. I'll have a revised version by tomorrow.

I looked at the deck too. The clinical benefits section is clear. My feedback: the comparison slide with competitor devices feels a bit aggressive. I'd soften it or remove it entirely—we don't want to give regulatory any reason to push back. Otherwise, looks good.

Agreed. I'll remove the direct competitor comparison and replace it with a neutral positioning slide. That's safer and still gets the message across. Now, on the sales script side—I've also drafted A3 (Standard Sales Script and Objection Guide) with opening, needs assessment, key messages and closing. The top 10 objections are documented with compliant responses. 36427, 438092, 96324—can you review and tell me if these responses feel natural or if they need tweaking?

I reviewed the script. It's comprehensive. The objection responses are good but some feel a bit formal. In my experience, clinicians respond better when we acknowledge their concern first before pivoting to the benefit. Maybe we could add a line like 'I understand that concern' before the response?
That's a smart adjustment. I'll add an empathy statement to each objection response. It'll make the script feel more conversational while staying compliant. 36427, any other feedback on A3?

The script is solid. One thing I'd add: a section on how to transition from the educational angle to the sales ask. Right now it jumps a bit. Also, can we include a quick reference on contraindications? That's critical for compliance and clinicians will ask.

Good points. I'll add a transition section and a contraindications reference card. Once I incorporate all this feedback, I'll send the revised A2 and A3 to regulatory affairs for formal review. That's a hard gate—we can't use anything until they sign off. Timeline: I'll have the revised versions ready for regulatory by EOD tomorrow, and we should expect their feedback by end of week.
That timeline works. Once regulatory approves, we'll need to do a quick training session so everyone is aligned on the messaging. Should we schedule that for next week?

Yes, let's plan the training for next week once we have regulatory sign-off. 70832, can you coordinate that as part of T9? In the meantime, let's assume D3 and D4 are on track pending regulatory review. Everyone good with that?
I haven't reviewed the deck yet. Should I do that too?
Yes, please. Take a look at A2 and A3 and let us know if anything is unclear or if you see any gaps. Your field perspective is valuable.

threads.thread_goal: Lock the digital outreach plan and webinar schedule.

messages.text: I've drafted the digital outreach plan (A4) for the pilot. The strategy focuses on LinkedIn and email for HCPs, with content themes around clinical education, case studies, and safety updates. I've also sketched out 4 pilot webinars targeting different specialties. Before we lock this in, I need feedback on: (1) which channels make sense for our accounts, (2) content frequency, and (3) webinar topics and dates. 36427, what's your read on which channels our target accounts actually use?

LinkedIn is solid for hospital decision-makers. Email is essential—that's how we reach the clinicians directly. I'd skip Twitter for this audience. On frequency: weekly email and 2-3 LinkedIn posts per week feels right. For webinars, I'd suggest we do one per week for the first month, targeting orthopedic, general surgery, and then a mixed specialty session. That gives us time to refine based on feedback.

Good. I'll update A4 to focus on LinkedIn and email, weekly cadence. For webinars, I'm thinking: Week 1 (Orthopedic), Week 2 (General Surgery), Week 3 (Mixed/Early Adopters). Each webinar will use the educational deck (A2) and include a Q&A. I'll prepare invitation templates and a follow-up sequence. Does that timeline work with the pilot account schedule?

Timeline looks good. One thing: we should coordinate the webinar invites with the sales team so we can do a soft outreach call first. That'll boost attendance. Also, can we make sure the webinar recordings are available for accounts that can't attend live?

Absolutely. I'll coordinate with 36427 on the soft outreach timing. And yes, we'll record and share the webinars within 24 hours. That also gives us content for email follow-ups. Let me finalize A4 with the channel mix, frequency, and webinar schedule by tomorrow. Then we can confirm D5 and D6.
I have a question: for the email content, should we be sending different messages to different specialties or the same message to everyone?

Good question. I'd recommend segmenting by specialty. The orthopedic group will care about different use cases than general surgery. We can use the same template but customize the clinical examples and benefits. That's more work upfront but will drive better engagement.
Agreed. Segmentation is worth it. 70832, once you finalize A4, can you also draft sample email templates so the team knows what we're sending? That'll help with the soft outreach calls too.

Will do. I'll include 3 sample emails (one per specialty) in A4. By tomorrow EOD, you'll have the full plan with channels, frequency, webinar dates, and email templates. Then we can lock D5 and D6 and move forward with scheduling.
Perfect. Once the webinar dates are locked, I'll coordinate with the sales team on the soft outreach calls. We should do those 3-5 days before each webinar.

Good plan. Let's reconvene tomorrow once A4 is finalized. We'll confirm D5 and D6, lock the webinar schedule, and assign owners for the soft outreach calls. This will keep us on track for the 21-day pilot launch.

threads.thread_goal: Align on CRM logging, KPIs and reporting expectations.

messages.text: I've prepared the KPI tracking template (A6) and a draft CRM logging process (A8). The template tracks leads, demos, orders, and feedback during the pilot. The CRM process defines which fields are required for each new device interaction. Before we roll this out, I need alignment on: (1) which KPIs we're actually measuring, (2) how we define each one, and (3) what minimum data we capture per CRM entry. 36427, can you review and flag any gaps?

I've reviewed both. A6 looks comprehensive. The KPIs are clear: leads, demos, orders, and feedback. One thing: we should also track 'no-decision' outcomes—those are valuable for understanding objections. On A8, the CRM fields are good, but I'd add a 'next step' field so we know what the follow-up action is. That'll help with consistency.

Good points. I'll add 'no-decision' as a lead outcome and add the 'next step' field to A8. That'll give us better visibility into the pipeline. Now, on definitions: should we define a 'lead' as any contact with a clinician, or only those who express interest?

I'd say a lead is anyone we've had a substantive conversation with about the device. That includes webinar attendees and people we've called. That way we capture the full funnel and can see conversion rates at each stage.
Agreed. And a 'demo' is when we've done a hands-on or detailed product walkthrough. An 'order' is when they've committed to purchase. That's clear and measurable.

Perfect. I'll document those definitions in the first tab of A6. Now, on CRM logging: what's the minimum data we need per entry? I'm thinking: account name, contact name, date, interaction type (call/webinar/email), outcome, and next step. Does that cover it?
I'd also add a 'notes' field so we can capture specific questions or concerns. That'll help when we're analyzing feedback later.

Good idea. I'll add a 'notes' field. So the minimum data per CRM entry is: account, contact, date, interaction type, outcome, next step, and notes. I'll also create a quick-reference checklist (A5) so everyone knows what to log and when. That should reduce errors and inconsistency.
A5 is a good idea. We should also do a quick training on how to use the CRM fields. Can that be part of the broader training session next week?

Absolutely. I'll include a CRM walkthrough in T9 (the internal training session). By tomorrow EOD, I'll have A6, A8, and A5 finalized with all the feedback. Then we can confirm D7 and D8, and we'll be ready to launch the tracking system.

Perfect. Once we have D7 and D8 locked, we'll also need to set up a weekly reporting cadence. I'm thinking: every Monday, we pull the KPI data from A6 and share a summary in the channel. That keeps everyone aligned on progress and flags any issues early.

Good plan. I'll set up the weekly summary as a channel ritual. That'll be part of the post-launch cadence. Let's reconvene tomorrow once A5, A6, and A8 are finalized. We'll confirm D7 and D8, and then we're ready to train the team and go live with tracking.

threads.thread_goal: Share pilot results, feedback and decide on broader rollout.

messages.text: Pilot wrap-up time. We've completed 3 weeks of outreach across our 8 pilot accounts. Early numbers are solid: 24 leads generated, 8 demos completed, 2 orders placed. More importantly, we've gathered a lot of feedback on the messaging and process. I've consolidated the key insights and linked the post-pilot report (A7) below. Before we decide on full rollout, let's review what worked, what didn't, and what we need to adjust. 70832, can you walk us through the report?

Thanks for pulling that together. A7 shows some really positive signals. The webinars had strong attendance (avg 12 per session) and the educational approach resonated. The main feedback themes: (1) clinicians want more case studies, (2) the sales script felt a bit stiff in some calls, and (3) email frequency was right but content could be more targeted. On the negative side, we had 3 accounts that didn't engage at all—those are worth analyzing separately.

I agree on the case studies. That's something we can add quickly. On the script, I think the issue was that some reps were reading it verbatim instead of using it as a guide. We should emphasize that in the training. The 3 non-engaged accounts—were those the ones we flagged as 'new relationships' at the start?

Yes, exactly. The non-engaged accounts were all new relationships. That tells us we should prioritize warm accounts for the next wave. Also, the 2 orders came from accounts where we had existing relationships and did multiple touchpoints. That's a key insight for scaling.
So for the next phase, should we focus on the warm accounts first and then expand to new relationships? That might give us better conversion rates.

That makes sense. Let's use the pilot learnings to refine our account strategy. I'm proposing we update A1 to reflect what we've learned and prioritize warm accounts for the next wave. That's part of D1 (reconfirm or adjust target account strategy). On the script side, we need to decide if A3 needs changes or if it's just a training/coaching issue. 70832, what's your read?

I think A3 is solid, but we should add more flexibility language and emphasize the case study approach. The script is a guide, not a word-for-word read. I'd also add a section on how to handle the 'we need to think about it' objection—that came up a lot. So minor tweaks to A3, but mostly it's about coaching reps to use it conversationally. That's D4 (decide whether to keep or update the sales script).
I agree. The script is good; it's execution. Let's do a quick coaching session with the team before the next wave. We can use real examples from the pilot to show what worked.

Good idea. So here's my proposal: (1) Update A1 to prioritize warm accounts based on pilot learnings—that's D1. (2) Keep A3 but add the 'think about it' objection and emphasize conversational use—that's D4. (3) Add case studies to the deck and email content. (4) Do a coaching session next week. Everyone good with that?

Sounds good. I'll update A1 with the warm account prioritization and add the case studies to A2 and the email templates. I'll also revise A3 with the new objection and coaching notes. By end of week, we'll have everything ready for the next wave.
This is helpful. So we're moving forward with the full rollout then?

Yes, we're moving forward. The pilot validated the approach. We'll expand to the next tier of accounts starting next week, using the refined strategy and materials. 70832 will have the updates ready by end of week, and we'll do the coaching session before we launch the next wave.

Perfect. I'll also prepare a summary of the pilot learnings (T11 is complete) and share it in the channel. That way everyone understands what we learned and why we're making these adjustments. The full rollout strategy will be clear and data-driven.
